cards.title: One lap decides the whole race
cards.text: 22 cars, three rounds: 6 out after the first, 6 after the second, and ten left to fight for the grid that shapes everything the race can become.

cards.title: Out before it got serious
cards.text: Colapinto (P17), Gasly (P18), Stroll (P19), Bottas (P20), Perez (P21), Bortoleto (P22).

cards.title: So close to the top ten
cards.text: Hamilton (P11), Piastri (P12), Câmara (P13), Lindblad (P14), Sainz (P15), Verstappen (P16, no time set in this round).

cards.title: 9 laps thrown in the bin
cards.text: In qualifying a deleted lap can be the difference between Q3 and going home early.

cards.title: Hamilton and Hadjar were quickest through the trap: 266 km/h
cards.text: Top speed says as much about wing level and the tow from the car ahead as it does about the engine.

cards.title: Nobody owned the whole lap
cards.text: The quickest sectors of the session were split between two drivers, so the ideal lap was never actually driven.

cards.title: Yellow flags out 7 times, and the session stopped 2 times
cards.text: A red flag stops the session and sends everybody back to the pits.

cards.title: How the race starts
cards.text: P1 Norris · P2 Antonelli · P3 Lawson · P4 Hulkenberg · P5 Hadjar · P6 Bearman
bullets: Bottas did not start, so 21 cars took the start
Russell qualified P2 and starts P7, 5 places further back
Leclerc qualified P4 and starts P14, 10 places further back
Lindblad qualified P14 and starts P18, 4 places further back
Hamilton qualified P11 and starts P20, 9 places further back
The grid is not the qualifying order. A penalty moves a car back, whether for something on track or for a new engine, and everybody behind it moves up
